findings.finding: The Approach frames the shared cascade_parent_first as owning the TOCTOU re-check and the ConcurrencyMismatch-preserving error rewrap, but the inbound reconciler cascade (apply_inbound_events.py:149-201) deliberately has NEITHER — it uses _write_event_file (not transition_compute, to dodge the start-work gate and eager commit/push), walks iteratively returning event paths, and has no benign-race re-check because it is a single-threaded batch. Routing the inbound path through a helper carrying interactive-only TOCTOU/rewrap machinery would be a golden-hammer over-fit of an interactive-verb abstraction onto a batch-orchestration seam. The plan should make explicit that only the DECISION (_CASCADING_EDGES + _resolve_parent_in_status, already shared by 2044) is what the inbound path reuses, keeping the interactive-only TOCTOU/rewrap out of it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the op-invoking `cascade_parent_first` design against Gerrit 2044's gate-free/push-free inbound writer in the Approach section: state that the sharable layer across all three sites is the DECISION (`_CASCADING_EDGES` + `_resolve_parent_in_status`), and that the op-invoking wrapper is the claim/transition surface only.
evidence: Approach: "`claim_compute` passes `op=claim_compute` ... `transition_compute` passes itself" — the helper invokes the interactive verb recursively

despotic-prime-reindeer (2044, merged commit d38c41b22c) Approach: "Deliberately do NOT route inbound status through `transition_compute`: ... would subject Jira-originated moves to the start-work plan-review gate (an LLM gate) and to eager per-event commit/push ... The cascade DECISION (edge table + parent eligibility) is shared; only the write primitive differs"

The consolidation the plan seeks (one implementation) cannot cover all three sites via an op-invoking helper; the sharable layer across all three is the DECISION (edge table + eligibility lookup), not the op-invoking cascade body
findings.finding: The Approach designs the shared helper as op-invoking (cascade_parent_first calls op=claim_compute / op=transition_compute recursively), but Gerrit 2044 (despotic-prime-reindeer, merged) deliberately shares only the cascade DECISION (_CASCADING_EDGES + _resolve_parent_in_status) at the inbound reconcile writer and explicitly does NOT route through transition_compute — because that would subject Jira-originated moves to the LLM start-work gate and eager per-event commit/push. An op-invoking helper is therefore structurally incompatible with folding in the inbound writer, so the third call site cannot join the same shared implementation the plan proposes. The Approach section never reconciles this; only AC4 hedges it.
findings.location: Approach section (`transition_compute` passes itself / `claim_compute` passes `op=claim_compute`); AC line 4
scenarios: Implementer tries to fold the inbound writer through cascade_parent_first and reintroduces the gate/push the reconciler must avoid

Implementer concludes the inbound site must stay separate and AC4's 'records why it stays separate' is satisfied only ad hoc, leaving the edge table still shared but the cascade body duplicated in spirit
findings.suggested_fix: In Approach, split the consolidation into two layers: (1) a shared decision layer (the single `_CASCADING_EDGES` table + `_resolve_parent_in_status`) that all three sites consult — which 2044's inbound writer already does; (2) the op-invoking `cascade_parent_first` wrapper used only by claim/transition. Then AC4 becomes 'the inbound writer shares the decision layer; it stays a separate writer by design (2044's gate/push constraint)' rather than an open OR.
